subject.title: Standardize async resource lifecycle management across retry/cleanup paths

question: Should OpenClaw add a shared async resource lifecycle/shutdown API across agent, gateway, and plugin cleanup paths, and which boundary should own it?
rationale: The issue is not a single broken code path; it would create or reshape core/plugin SDK lifecycle contracts and decide whether targeted fixes remain the preferred pattern.

options.title: Define a narrow shared lifecycle seam
options.body: Add a backward-compatible, owner-scoped lifecycle/drain API and prove it on one agent cleanup path plus one plugin/gateway path before broader migration.

options.title: Keep targeted lifecycle fixes
options.body: Continue fixing concrete races in their owning subsystems and close this tracker once the remaining symptoms are represented by narrower issues.

options.title: Defer until another concrete race appears
options.body: Leave current guards in place and revisit a shared API only when a new unfixed race shows that existing hooks cannot express the needed cleanup ordering.

recommendation.title: Define a narrow shared lifecycle seam
recommendation.body: Add a backward-compatible, owner-scoped lifecycle/drain API and prove it on one agent cleanup path plus one plugin/gateway path before broader migration.

likelyOwner.reason: This account has the strongest recent history across outbound recovery/storage, current lifecycle code ownership signals, and prior maintainer-facing direction for related design items.
